layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The Segment Anything Model (SAM) stands as a foundational framework for im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: age segmentation. While it exhibits remarkable zero-shot generalization in typical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scenarios, its advantage diminishes when applied to specialized domains like med-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ical imagery and remote sensing. To address this limitation, this paper introduces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Conv-LoRA, a simple yet effective parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach. By

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: integrating ultra-lightweight convolutional parameters into Low-Rank Adaptation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (LoRA), Conv-LoRA can inject image-related inductive biases into the plain ViT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoder, further reinforcing SAM's local prior assumption. Notably, Conv-LoRA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not only preserves SAM's extensive segmentation knowledge but also revives its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capacity of learning high-level image semantics, which is constrained by SAM's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: foreground-background segmentation pretraining. Comprehensive experimenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion across diverse benchmarks spanning multiple domains underscores Conv-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: LoRA's superiority in adapting SAM to real-world semantic segmentation tasks.¹

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The AI community have witnessed the explosion development of a series of foundation models in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recent years, such as CLIP (Radford et al., 2021), GPT-4 (OpenAI, 2023) and ViT-22B (Dehghani

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2023). Recently, Segment Anything (SAM) (Kirillov et al., 2023), a promptable model pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trained on over 1 billion masks and 11 million images, emerged as a foundation model for image seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation. Despite its impressive zero-shot performance on generic object segmentation, it doesn't

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: perform well on many real-world segmentation tasks in certain domains (Tang et al., 2023; Ji et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2023; Zhou et al., 2023), such as natural images (Borji et al., 2019; Fan et al., 2020a), agriculture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Sriwastwa et al., 2018), remote sensing (Xu et al., 2018) and medical images (Fan et al., 2020b).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Following the pretraining-finetuing paradigm (Dosovitskiy et al., 2020; He et al., 2022; Liu et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2021a), it is natural to finetune SAM on downstream tasks to enhance its performance. However,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: existing works (Zhang & Liu, 2023; Chen et al., 2023; Shaharabany et al., 2023) have failed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: either analyze or address certain limitations inherent in SAM. 1) SAM's image encoder is a plain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ViT, which is known to lack of vision-specific inductive biases (Chen et al., 2022) that are useful

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for dense predictions. 2) SAM's pretraining is essentially a binary mask prediction task that, where,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: given one prompt, it separates foreground object from background. The low-level mask prediction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pretraining hinders SAM's ability to capture high-level image semantic information crucial for tasks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: like multi-class semantic segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To tackle the above limitations and still retain SAM's valuable segmentation knowledge acquired

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: during pretraining, we finetune a small set of (extra) model parameters while freezing most of SAM's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pretrained weights, hence parameter efficient finetuning (PEFT). This raises the question: Can PEFT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhance SAM encoder with image-related local prior and facilitate the acquisition of high-level

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semantic information?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we propose a new PEFT method named Conv-LoRA by diving into Low-Rank Adap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation (LoRA) (Hu et al., 2021). LoRA introduces slim trainable linear projection layers into each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transformer layer of SAM's encoder, thereby helping recover its capacity to extract high-level se-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mantic information. Our experiments demonstrate that LoRA surpasses the widely-adopted visual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompt tuning (VPT) (Jia et al., 2022), particularly in the multi-class semantic segmentation tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: On top of LoRA, Conv-LoRA integrates lightweight convolution layers within its bottleneck struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture. Convolution can introduce the image-related local prior (i.e. a pixel exhibits stronger correla-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion with its neighbors than the distant pixels) (Chen et al., 2022) through the local spatial operations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Furthermore, it is essential to inject the local prior into the appropriate scale(s) of image features,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: considering the potential variations in object scales. To this end, Conv-LoRA draws inspiration from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the concept of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) (Shazeer et al., 2017) and incorporates multiple parallel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolutional experts, each specializing in a distinct feature scale. Given that ViT processes image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: features at a fixed scale, typically downsampling them by a factor of 16 from the original resolution,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each expert in Conv-LoRA initially recovers image features at a specific scale, applies convolutional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operations, and then reverts the features to the default scale. Compared to ViT-adaptor (Chen et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2022) and vision-specific transformers like Swin Transformer (Liu et al., 2021a), Conv-LoRA pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vides an implicit way to enforce multi-scale local priors, assuming it can leverage image features at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the default scale to reconstruct feature information at higher scales. Fortunately, SAM's supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pretraining, which involves masks of various scales, enables the ViT to acquire knowledge of image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: features beyond the default scale.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the spirit of PEFT, we also remove the prompt encoder and add lightweight MLPs in the mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder for multi-class prediction. This simple modification has transformed SAM into an end-to-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: end model that can be finetuned on both binary and multi-class semantic segmentation applications.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Overall, our contribution can be summarized as follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We present an innovative PEFT technique Conv-LoRA. By incorporating supplementary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolution operations, Conv-LoRA reinforces the local prior of SAM from the perspective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of handling the limitation of plain ViT.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Conv-LoRA uses MoE to model the process of dynamically selecting the proper feature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scale to inject the vision-specific inductive biases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Our investigations reveal that SAM's pretraining has impeded its ViT encoder's capacity to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learn high-level image semantic information. However, LoRA demonstrates the potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to help SAM recover this crucial ability.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We conduct an extensive benchmark encompassing diverse domains, including natural im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages, agriculture, remote sensing, and healthcare. Conv-LoRA consistently exhibits supe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rior performance over other PEFT techniques in various downstream tasks.

layout_dets.text: 2 RELATED WORK

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT). Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) minimizes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computational and storage requirements by selectively fine-tuning a small subset of model param-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eters, while keeping the majority fixed. PEFT encompasses methods such as adapter-based tech-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: niques, selective parameter tuning, prompt-driven fine-tuning, and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: emerging from Natural Language Processing (NLP). In the adapter paradigm (Houlsby et al., 2019;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hu et al., 2021; Sung et al., 2022), compact modules are inserted within transformer layers, and other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approaches (Guo et al., 2020; Zaken et al., 2021) involve fine-tuning a small fraction of parameters

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from pre-trained backbones. Prompt tuning (Lester et al., 2021; Li & Liang, 2021) adds adaptable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tokens to input or intermediate sequences, and LoRA (Hu et al., 2021) introduces trainable low-rank

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matrices into transformer layers for weight updates.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: PEFT techniques have also proven effective in the Computer Vision (CV) domain. Visual Prompt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Tuning (VPT) (Jia et al., 2022) applies prompt tuning concepts (Lester et al., 2021) to image clas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sification, while Scale and Shift Feature Modulation (SSF) (Lian et al., 2022) uses scale and shift

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters for modulating visual features in image classifiers. Convpass (Jie & Deng, 2022) in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: troduces a convolutional bottleneck to enhance ViT's performance in image classification. In our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: study, we focus on developing PEFT for SAM in semantic segmentation tasks, specifically enforc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing multi-scale local priors beyond the default scale, distinguishing our approach from Convpass.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Segmentation Models. FCN (Long et al., 2015) is a key deep image segmentation model that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: directly generates pixel-wise segmentation maps from images. U-Net (Ronneberger et al., 2015)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: employs an encoder-decoder structure with skip connections to preserve fine-grained spatial infor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mation. Deeplab (Chen et al., 2017a) integrates atrous (dilated) convolutions for multi-scale context,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while PSPNet (Zhao et al., 2017) uses a pyramid pooling module. DANet (Fu et al., 2019), SANet

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Zhong et al., 2020), and EMA (Li et al., 2019) utilize attention mechanisms for contextual depen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dencies. Transformer architectures like PVT (Wang et al., 2021), Swin (Liu et al., 2021b), CvT (Wu

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2021), CoaT (Xu et al., 2021), LeViT (Graham et al., 2021), Segformer (Xie et al., 2021a),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and PVT v2 (Wang et al., 2022) bring various improvements. SAM (Ji et al., 2023), a recent break-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through in segmentation, offers a universal approach for segmenting diverse objects and regions in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images. Fine-tuning SAM on downstream tasks is recommended due to a lack of high-level semantic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information and potential domain bias in the pre-training dataset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fine-tuning SAM. Some prior works (Chen et al., 2023; Zhang & Liu, 2023; Wu et al., 2023; Chai

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2023; Shaharabany et al., 2023; Hu et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2023) explore fine-tuning SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for downstream tasks. These methods include tuning SAM's mask decoder or integrating parameter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: efficient tuning methods with SAM's image encoder. Some of them (e.g.,(Chen et al., 2023; Zhang

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: & Liu, 2023; Shaharabany et al., 2023)) provide end-to-end solutions to automate SAM. Our method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: further addresses the structural limitation of SAM's image encoder for capturing visual-specific in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ductive biases by introducing convolution operations. And we unveil that SAM's pretraining ham-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pers its ViT encoder's ability to learn high-level semantic information. We also transform SAM into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an end-to-end semantic segmentation model with minor architectural adjustments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mixture-of-Experts. Mixture-of-Expert (MoE) is designed to expand model capacity while in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: troducing small computational overhead. An MoE layer leverages multiple experts to enhance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model capacity, while using the gating network to regulate sparsity for computational savings. Feed-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Forward Networks (FFN) are commonly employed as the default choice for experts (Shazeer et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2017; Riquelme et al., 2021; Bao et al., 2022; Du et al., 2022; Zhou et al., 2022; Fedus et al., 2022).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Some efforts (Zuo et al., 2021; Zhou et al., 2022) focus on more efficient gating mechanisms.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In our work, we utilize the concept of MoE, not aiming at improving it. We compare MoE used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in our work with original MoE in three aspects: 1) The original goal of MoE is to expand model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capacity without excessively increasing computational overhead, whereas ours is to dynamically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inject the local prior into the feature maps of different scales. 2) The structures of experts in MoE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are typically the same, whereas ours are not. Each expert specializes in a specific scaling operation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Conv-LoRA aims to incorporate convolution operations between the encoder and decoder com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ponents of LoRA (fig. 2 (b)). On one hand, convolution can inject the image-related local prior,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A pivotal consideration in designing Conv-LoRA is determining the scale of feature maps at which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to introduce the local prior. While the feature maps in ViT are uniform in scale, object masks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: typically encompass a wide range of scales. Therefore, it is crucial to apply convolution operations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at the right scale. To tackle this challenge, we draw inspiration from the concept of Mixture of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Experts (MoE) (Shazeer et al., 2017). MoE comprises multiple expert networks and a gating module

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that dynamically selects which expert(s) to activate during the forward pass (fig. 3). Adapting this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concept to Conv-LoRA, each expert specializes in convolution at a specific scale of feature maps,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a compact gating module learns to dynamically choose the expert(s) based on the input data.

layout_dets.text: 3.2 END-TO-END MULTI-CLASS SEGMENTATION WITH SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM comprises three essential components: an image encoder, a prompt encoder, and a mask de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coder. When provided with an image and a prompt, which can take the form of a point, box, mask,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or text, the mask decoder generates a mask of the object associated with the given prompt. While

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this prompt-based approach renders SAM flexible for integration into larger systems, such as in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teractive segmentation or a combination of detection and subsequent segmentation, it does pose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenges in making SAM an end-to-end model in practical applications. To automate SAM, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: freeze the prompt encoder, thus always constant prompt tokens to mask decoder, when finetuning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it on downstream tasks. Moreover, the original mask decoder is designed to predict binary masks,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distinguishing between foreground and background based on the given prompt. To adapt SAM for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multi-class semantic segmentation tasks, we introduce a straightforward classification branch (de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: picted as the red dashed box in fig. 4) within the mask decoder. This extra branch is responsible for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predicting classification scores. Additionally, we apply full fine-tuning to the mask decoder as it is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a lightweight module. For more comprehensive information, refer to appendix B.

layout_dets.text: 4.3 ABLATION STUDY

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM's local prior assumption. SAM's local prior is grounded in its extensive segmentation pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training. Through supervised training on a vast dataset encompassing 1 billion high-quality masks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 11 million images, SAM has honed a robust capability to discern and capture local features

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within images. Notably, SAM's encoder retains the ViT architecture, which inherently lacks a ded-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: icated local prior. However, this deficiency is effectively compensated by the significant local

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prior acquired through segmentation pretraining.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We analyze using the mean attention distance as a metric. In fig. 5, SAM exhibits numerous heads

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the deep blocks with short mean attention distances, suggesting its heightened focus on local

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information during the later stages of the encoder. In contrast, the MAE pretrained ViT, representing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM's initialization, displays consistently long mean attention distances among attention heads

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the later stages. Consequently, SAM's segmentation pretraining induces a transformative shift

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in ViT's attention heads, steering them from a global-oriented to a local-oriented configuration.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This transformation underscores the efficacy of SAM's approach in imbuing the model with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distinctive local prior, enhancing its ability to capture fine-grained details within images.

layout_dets.text: 5 CONCLUSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Parameter efficient finetuning (PEFT) is a popular way when adapting foundation models to var-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ious downstream tasks. We present Conv-LoRA, a novel PEFT approach for applying SAM to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: downstream segmentation applications. Conv-LoRA is simple, generic, and obtains promising re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sults over multiple domains including natural images, agriculture, remote sensing, and healthcare

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Moreover, ours shed light on several aspects of SAM: 1) although the large-scale supervised seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation pretraining can provide image-related local prior knowledge from the data perspective,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: injecting lightweight convolution operations in the ViT encoder can further boost the exploitation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of local prior from another perspective of architecture; 2) the foreground-background segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pretraining prevents the image encoder from learning high-level semantic information, which can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be alleviated through finetuning relatively few parameters in the encoder.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our efforts primarily focus on developing a general PEFT method for SAM, showing stronger per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formance than existing PEFT methods in a broad spectrum of benchmarks, other than directly com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: peting with state-of-the-art (SOTA) models in specialized domains. Given that SAM fine-tuned with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Conv-LoRA may not yet consistently outperform domain-specific SOTA models, we believe that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tailoring the mask decoder and prompt encoder beyond image encoder finetuning, and combining

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Conv-LoRA with other PEFT methods can be promising directions for domain-specific applications.

layout_dets.text: B MASK DECODER FOR MULTI-CLASS SEGMENTATION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM's mask decoder follows the design in mask-based segmentation, wherein the image is grouped

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into N (i.e., the number of output tokens in fig. 4) regions represented by binary masks. How-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ever, unlike other mask-based methods such as Maskformer (Cheng et al., 2021) and Mask2former

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Cheng et al., 2022), SAM does not incorporate a classification module; it solely identifies the fore-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground, lacking the ability for multi-class segmentation. What we need to do is straightforward:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: incorporate a classification branch to obtain class predictions for the corresponding N masks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: During training, we need to match the set of N mask predictions and the set of ground truth seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments. We follow the design in Mask2Former (Cheng et al., 2022), which proposes a memory-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: friendly way for bipartite matching between the predictions and ground truths. It efficiently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alleviates the memory demands in semantic segmentation tasks that necessitate high-resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask prediction, particularly for SAM involving the processing of high-resolution input images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1024 × 1024). For the masks that are not allocated to any ground truths, an extra ‘no object'

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: category is introduced to ensure the one-to-one matching. Hence, the classification branch should

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: produce

layout_dets.text: class predictions, assuming there are originally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: categories. For semantic infer-

layout_dets.text: ence, we can exclude the no object' category and perform a straightforward matrix multiplication

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between the masks and the classification predictions to obtain pixel-wise predictions.

layout_dets.text: C DATASET DETAILS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Polyp Segmentation (medical images) Polyp Segmentation, the task to identify abnormal growths

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: known as polyps within gastrointestinal endoscopic images, plays a critical role in early colorectal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cancer diagnosis and treatment planning, and it presents a formidable challenge due to the consid-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erable diversity in polyp shapes and sizes. We choose two polyp segmentation datasets: Kvasir (Jha

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2020) and CVC-ClinicDB/CVC-612 (Bernal et al., 2015). Kvasir contains 1000 images and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CVC-ClinicDB, also called CVC-612, includes 612 open-access images. Fan et al. (2020b) divides

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the images into a 9:1 ratio for training and testing. Additionally, we randomly divide a validation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: set comprising 20% of the images from the training set, for validation during training. Furthermore,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we also use images from CVC-ColonDB (Tajbakhsh et al., 2015), EndoScene (Vázquez et al., 2017)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and ETIS (Silva et al., 2014) for testing following the setting in (Fan et al., 2020b). We consistently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: train all methods for 30 epochs, unless otherwise specified for specific datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Skin Lesion Segmentation (medical images) Skin Lesion Segmentation involves the segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of various types of skin lesions within medical images, serving a crucial role in the early diagnosis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and treatment of skin disorders, notably skin cancer. However, this task is particularly challenging

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: due to ambiguous boundaries and color variations. We choose ISIC 2017 (Codella et al., 2018) for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: skin lesion segmentation. ISIC 2017 provides 2000 images for training, 150 images for validation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 600 images for testing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Camouflaged Object Segmentation (natural images) Camouflaged Object Segmentation focuses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on identifying objects that are concealed within complex or visually cluttered backgrounds, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is more challenging comparing to traditional object segmentation. We choose three camouflaged

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object detection datasets: COD10K (Fan et al., 2020a), CHAMELEON (Skurowski et al., 2018), and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CAMO (Le et al., 2019). COD10K contains 3040 training and 2026 testing samples. CHAMELEON

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: includes 76 images collected from the Internet for testing. And CAMO provides 1000 images for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training and 250 for testing. Following (Fan et al., 2020a), we train on the combined dataset consists

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the training images from COD10K and CAMO for 20 epochs, and test on the three datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Addtionally, we randomly split 10% of the images from the training set for validation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Shadow Detection (natural images) Shadow Detection focuses on the recognition of shadow re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gions within a scene and can facilitate the estimation of lighting conditions or the removal of shad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ows. We choose SBU (Vicente et al., 2016), which is the largest annotated shadow dataset. SBU

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contains 4085 and 638 images for training and testing. We randomly split 10% of the images from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the training set for validation and we train the methods for 10 epochs with balanced binary cross

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entropy loss.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Leaf Segmentation (agriculture) Leaf segmentation involves the identification of individual plant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leaves within agricultural images and plays a crucial role in advancing automation for plant diseases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: control and high quality food production. We choose a Leaf Disease Segmentation dataset (Rath,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2023), which contains 498 images for training and 90 images for testing. We randomly split the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training images into 80% for training, 20% for validation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Road Segmentation (remote sensing) Road segmentation detects road or street regions within im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages or video frames, and is crucial for applications in autonomous driving, traffic analysis, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: urban planning. We choose Massachusetts Roads Dataset (Mnih, 2013), which contains 1107 im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages for training, 13 images for validation and 48 images for testing. And we train the methods for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 20 epochs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Multiclass Semantic Segmentation (natural images) We choose Trans10K-v1 (Xie et al., 2020) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Trans10K-v2 (Xie et al., 2021b) dataset for multi-class transparent object segmentation. Trans10K-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: v1 dataset contains 10428 images, with background as one category and two more categories of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transparent objects: Transparent Things (e.g., cups, bottles) and Stuff (e.g., windows). Trans10K-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: v2 dataset is based on Trans10K-v1 dataset, with more fine-grained categories annotations. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset contains background plus two main categories divided into 11 fine-grained categories: 1)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Transparent Things containing cup, bottle, jar, bowl and eyeglass. 2) Transparent Stuff containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: windows, shelf, box, freezer, glass walls and glass doors. In respect to fine-grained categories and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high diversity, Trans10K-v2 is more challenging than Trans10K-v1. All the datasets use 5000, 1000

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 4428 images for training, validation and testing, respectively.

layout_dets.text: it probably can't bring local prior into features of larger scales than the default. The features in ViT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are downscaled 16x from the original image, so injecting priors in larger scale features are generally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more useful, as evidenced in table 4, where the optimal scale is usually larger than the default scale.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Computational Cost. In table 14, we compare the training / inference speed and per epoch training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time with the ISIC 2017 dataset and a single V100 GPU. While Conv-LoRA is slower in speed than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: others, it achieves robust performance gains across various semantic segmentation tasks (table 1).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We find that the main cost comes from the upscale and downscale operations. A possible future

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: direction is exploring how to inject local prior without explicitly scaling up and down features. We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also notice that there are some other orthogonal works, like token merging (Liang et al., 2022; Bolya

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2022), that may accelerate Conv-LoRA.

layout_dets.text: F LOCAL PRIOR ANALYSIS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We elaborate on SAM's local prior assumption' mentioned in our abstract in section 4.3. Addition-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ally, as our Conv-LoRA is designed to reinforce existing inductive biases within the features, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: investigate the presence of these biases in the features.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We use two metrics: 1) Mean attention distance, which reflects the extent of local or global in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formation that a self-attention layer is aggregating (Dosovitskiy et al., 2020; Raghu et al., 2021).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We calculate the attention distance for each attention head, defined as the average distance between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the position of the query patch and the locations to which it attends, weighted by the attention

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: weights. Then we calculate the average attention distance for each layer by computing the mean

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: across 500 randomly sampled images from downstream semantic segmentation tasks. 2) Relative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: log amplitudes (Park & Kim, 2022), which reflects whether the model tends to reduce or amplify

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high-frequency signals (e.g., edges, textures) in feature map. We compute the relative log ampli-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tudes of the Fourier-transformed feature map in each layer and average them across layers. Then we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: calculate the mean of the relative log amplitudes over 100 randomly sampled segmentation images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Inductive biases of the features. Extensive pre-training on large-scale datasets has been demon-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strated to equip ViTs with inductive biases (Dosovitskiy et al., 2020; Raghu et al., 2021). SAM's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large-scale segmentation pretraining further amplifies these inductive biases within the features.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To evaluate the inductive biases of the features, we conduct comprehensive comparisons among

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: randomly initialized ViT, MAE pretrained ViT, and SAM ViT. We use mean attention distance and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relative log amplitudes for evaluation. In fig. 7, as the training progresses from randomly initialized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ViT to MAE ViT and ultimately to SAM ViT, we observe a consistent trend: the mean attention

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distance decreases, while the high-frequency signals in the features increase, indicating a focus on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: local information. These findings further confirm the presence of inductive biases in features

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: following large-scale pre-training. Furthermore, the findings affirm the rationality of Conv-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: LoRA in reinforcing the inherent inductive biases within the features.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Convolutional layers could introduce inductive biases, thereby enhancing data efficiency during fine-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tuning. Therefore, we undertake experiments in a low-data regime to validate whether Conv-LoRA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can indeed improve data efficiency in semantic segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Specifically, we conduct experiments under the few-shot setting, wherein acquiring data for down-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stream tasks is challenging, and only a limited number of training samples per task are available.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
